initial_findings: The first codec draft used local doctor and audit budgets instead of the shared application limits, accepted terminal rows in open-session projections, and emitted fractional seconds unlike the released macOS Internet-date-time encoder.

The first handler draft supplied Cache-Control as an extra asset header even though the response encoder owns and emits that policy, causing otherwise valid shell/static responses to close as bounded 500 errors.
corrections: The codec now uses the shared 128-check, 512 KiB audit/doctor, and identity budgets; validates Domain::isOpen for open collections; requires nonzero identity/presence process identifiers; and emits second-resolution timestamps.
Asset dispatch now supplies no cache-control extra header and relies on the response encoder's single no-store policy. Every released route then passed the concrete boundary suite.
independent_review.post_correction_result: Two independent source/test reviews found no remaining application-boundary P1/P2 issue. An additional CodeRabbit CLI review was attempted but unavailable because its installer rejects this Windows host and no WSL distribution is installed; it produced no source assessment and no repository changes.

behavior_proved: the application boundary is final and noncopyable, owns immutable listener-generation policy/identity values, and depends only on injected transport-neutral ports
all released shell, static, telemetry, status, operational, manager, settings, control, and shutdown routes dispatch through one closed route switch

telemetry aliases use one owned observation per request, reject a successful null observation safely, and SSE subscription ownership closes exactly once on capacity, invalid-rate, or response-boundary failure

application JSON preserves released field names, null/omission behavior, agent-body exclusion, second-resolution UTC timestamps, and exact prune and shutdown acknowledgements

manager shutdown is not called during prepare; the acknowledgement owns only RequestManagerShutdown, which executes after delivery with a fresh context and propagates post-delivery failure
all response and source limits reject rather than truncate, including open-session semantics and the 20/40/80/100 status/session/audit/diagnostic collection caps
